headline: Committee discusses taxicab baggage charges in Bill 101 (2026)

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: Bill 101 would raise the general baggage charge from 50 cents to $1 per piece per trip and allow a $10 charge for certain oversized or heavy items. Members proposed amendments, and the chair said the bill will move on for first reading.
meeting.recap: The committee took up a taxicab rates report and Bill 101 (2026) on taxicab baggage charges.[[0:16:30]] Bill 101 would raise the general baggage charge from 50 cents to $1 per piece per trip.[[0:17:34]] It would also allow a $10 charge for certain oversized or heavy items and some equipment.[[0:17:43]] The finance director said the department reviewed Bill 101 and had no comments or concerns.[[0:18:36]] One person testified, asking if Native Hawaiian and Kanaka Maoli people could be free of these charges.[[0:21:11]] A member asked who enforces taxi rates.[[0:22:29]] A finance staff member said the DMV issues licenses, and county code is enforced by a Maui police enforcement division.[[0:23:05]] The same staff member said Maui's regular baggage rate appears lowest among the counties.[[0:27:20]] The chair moved to pass Bill 101 on first reading.[[0:28:45]] A member proposed an amendment rewording section D, which covers the $1 and $10 charges.[[0:29:08]] Members voted aye on that amendment, with no count given.[[0:31:56]] Another amendment was proposed so oversized baggage means 50 pounds or more, not more than 50 pounds.[[0:32:44]] The committee approved the bill as amended.[[0:39:18]] The chair said the bill will move on for first reading.[[0:39:33]]
meeting.next: The chair said the bill will move on for first reading. The chair said she will give a taxi operator who called her a PUC contact for his license concerns.

moments.q: "Can the Native Hawaiian and Kanaka Maoli people be free of charge of any of these things?"
